turns.en: Today, I'm joined by Marvin Schwaibold, who leads the product design studio at Shopify. He'll give us a behind-the-scenes look at his process, where we'll see how he's using the latest AI tools to bring his designs to life, then review some viewer-submitted websites. Welcome to another episode of Design Review. Marvin, thanks for joining us.
turns.zh: 今天，我邀请到了 Marvin Schwaibold，他负责领导 Shopify 的产品设计工作室。他将带我们深入了解他的工作流程，展示他如何使用最新的 AI 工具将设计变为现实，然后我们会点评一些观众提交的网站。欢迎来到另一期《设计评论》。Marvin，感谢你的参与。

turns.en: Thank you for having me.
turns.zh: 感谢邀请我。

turns.en: Before we get into your work at Shopify, I'd love to hear more about your process and the tools that you're using today to design with AI.
turns.zh: 在我们讨论你在 Shopify 的工作之前，我很想了解更多关于你的工作流程以及你今天用来进行 AI 设计的工具。

turns.en: I feel like the process itself hasn't really changed. It's still extremely iterative and sequenced out. There's a lot of iterations and variations in the work in and of itself, but the tooling has definitely shifted a lot from tools like Figma and working with aesthetic layouts into more of an AI-driven workflow, where I'll use Figma as a scratch pad for some of the ideas I have, but then very quickly that'll transcend into real demos that I can use, and then I only piggyback back into Figma from time to time if I need to lay something out or explain something to AI, but it's definitely more of a world now that includes tools like Codex and Claude Code and being in terminal a lot and just getting to an output that I can use and test on my phone or computer a lot faster, and that becomes like a really fun still very iterative cycle, but we've definitely moved away from the canvas more to like AI tools in general.
turns.zh: 我觉得流程本身并没有真正改变。它仍然非常迭代和有序。工作中本身就有很多迭代和变体，但工具确实发生了很大变化，从 Figma 和美学布局工具转向更多 AI 驱动的工作流程，我会用 Figma 作为草稿本记录一些想法，但很快这些想法就会转化为我可以使用的真实演示，然后我只会偶尔回到 Figma 来布局或向 AI 解释某些东西，但现在绝对是一个包含 Codex 和 Claude Code 等工具的世界，经常在终端中工作，只是更快地得到我可以在手机或电脑上使用和测试的输出，这变成了一个非常有趣的仍然非常迭代的循环，但我们肯定已经从画布转向更多 AI 工具。

turns.en: And how much of that workflow is AI driving a lot of the process and how much of it is you the human?
turns.zh: 那么，这个工作流程中有多少是 AI 在驱动大部分过程，有多少是你人类在驱动？

turns.en: I think it's a lot of me the human driving AI to do a lot of the heavy lifting for me, but there's a lot of quality controls, decision-making that are all up to the designers. We're in the driving seat, and we're actually more than ever now in a position where the output isn't the issue anymore, it's us being extremely selective about what we go forward with and what we work with. So, it's a lot more curating what AI is creating and that is a continuous back and forth with AI. I feel like AI is extremely capable of getting a lot of things done that we needed to do as long as you understand the complexity of what it is that you're working on and you're able to break that down into a multitude of almost like subtasks that then you can feed to the agent bit by bit. And then it's a back and forth.
turns.zh: 我认为很大程度上是我这个人类在驱动 AI 为我完成很多繁重的工作，但有很多质量控制和决策都取决于设计师。我们坐在驾驶座上，实际上我们现在比以往任何时候都处于这样一个位置：输出不再是问题，而是我们要极其选择性地决定我们继续推进什么、使用什么。所以，更多的是对 AI 创造的内容进行策展，这是一个与 AI 持续来回的过程。我觉得 AI 非常擅长完成很多我们需要做的事情，只要你理解你正在处理的复杂性，并且能够将其分解成多个几乎像子任务一样的东西，然后你可以一点一点地喂给智能体。然后就是来回互动。

turns.en: And it sounds like a lot of what you're describing is that your role is actually to be the editor.
turns.zh: 听起来你所描述的很多内容都表明你的角色实际上是编辑。

turns.en: We're more the editors now than ever before, which is I think fun. That's great. I mean, that was always the role, but getting to the point of editing just took a lot of hand-crafted design that we would do in Figma and just more and more of that can be now sped up and extrapolated with AI tooling.
turns.zh: 我们现在比以往任何时候都更像是编辑，我觉得这很有趣。那很棒。我的意思是，这一直是角色所在，但达到编辑这一步之前需要大量手工设计，我们会在 Figma 中做这些，而现在越来越多的工作可以通过 AI 工具加速和推断。

turns.en: And so, you the human are still responsible for the ultimate final output and making sure that it meets your bar.
turns.zh: 所以，你作为人类仍然要对最终输出负责，并确保它达到你的标准。

turns.en: Always.
turns.zh: 总是如此。

turns.en: But you have all these tools now to be able to get there way faster.
turns.zh: 但现在你拥有所有这些工具，能够更快地达到目标。

turns.en: 100%. I mean, AI has definitely raised the ceiling for all of us, but it's not a crafter. It can execute complexity and technology that I couldn't handwrite code. It can write code, but it doesn't know what looks good and what looks bad and that's for me to decide and to steer AI into the right direction.
turns.zh: 100%。我的意思是，AI 肯定为我们所有人提高了上限，但它不是工匠。它可以执行复杂性和技术，而我无法手写代码。它可以写代码，但它不知道什么好看什么不好看，这由我决定，并引导 AI 走向正确的方向。

turns.en: I've been a big fan of your work for a long time. So, maybe first just start off and tell us about the product design studio at Shopify and what you guys do there.
turns.zh: 我一直是你的作品的忠实粉丝。所以，也许首先请告诉我们 Shopify 的产品设计工作室以及你们在那里做什么。

turns.en: I work with a team of very talented designers. We've been there for the last year and between us we basically run an initiative at the company to redesign and touch the most important surfaces we have. So, from anything related to Sidekick, which is our AI infrastructure layers that basically manage our entire admin to the mobile app, which we call the green app, and everything from admin and admin dashboards we look at and work with. Quite recently have been working with a lot of new AI infrastructure that the engineering teams have built for us, and yeah, it's just been a really exciting last year.
turns.zh: 我与一支非常有才华的设计师团队合作。过去一年我们一直在那里，我们基本上在公司内发起了一项倡议，重新设计并触及我们最重要的界面。所以，从与 Sidekick 相关的任何内容——Sidekick 是我们的 AI 基础设施层，基本上管理我们整个后台——到我们称之为绿色应用的移动应用，以及我们查看和处理的从后台到后台仪表盘的一切。最近一直在与工程团队为我们构建的许多新 AI 基础设施合作，是的，过去一年真的非常令人兴奋。

turns.en: Yeah, it's actually really interesting cuz Shopify is like two decades old or something at this point, right?
turns.zh: 是的，这真的很有趣，因为 Shopify 到现在大概有二十年历史了，对吧？

turns.en: 20 years old.
turns.zh: 20 年了。

turns.en: 20 years old, and so we are
turns.zh: 20 年了，所以我们

turns.en: 21, I think, actually.
turns.zh: 实际上，我想是 21 年了。

turns.en: Yeah, we're in a new era now. AI is changing a lot of things, and it sounds like a lot of the work that you're doing is actually to modernize and bring it into a modern era, which is through design, but also the experience itself, right? Like, what is the design team in your product design studio actually work on there? Are you just, you know, in Figma and canvases and designs and passing them off to engineers, or what is the design function like that you manage there?
turns.zh: 是的，我们现在处于一个新时代。AI 正在改变很多事情，听起来你做的很多工作实际上是为了现代化并将其带入现代时代，这通过设计实现，但也包括体验本身，对吧？比如，你产品设计工作室的设计团队实际上在那里做什么？你们只是，你知道，在 Figma 和画布和设计中，然后将它们交给工程师，或者你管理的设计职能是什么样的？

turns.en: At least at the moment, there's almost like two parts of this big initiative that we're taking. Part of the organization of the design team has redesigned the entire admin experience. This redesign starts in Figma and with polishing interfaces and bringing that into the web, and the other part of the organization, the Sidekick team of Shopify, is working on automating and manipulating a lot of the Shopify interfaces via the chat, so that you can use chat, Sidekick, or AI infra to basically manage your store and automate a lot of what it means to be a merchant online. And that's like they're basically two almost controversial, paradoxic sectors of the company, but they work really well together. So, you're building really beautiful new UI, but you're also using new UI to basically generate AI infra and AI workflows, and that's like incredible to see. And a lot of that actually translates very nicely back into the mobile app, and is up-leveling the mobile experience as well. It's a lot more conversational and a lot more talking to Sidekick about your business than having to manipulate your business via the interface.
turns.zh: 至少目前，我们正在进行的这项大倡议几乎有两个部分。设计团队的一部分重新设计了整个后台体验。这个重新设计从 Figma 开始，打磨界面并将其带入网络，而组织的另一部分，Shopify 的 Sidekick 团队，正在通过聊天自动化和操作许多 Shopify 界面，这样你可以使用聊天、Sidekick 或 AI 基础设施来基本上管理你的商店，并自动化很多在线商家的工作。这几乎是公司内两个几乎有争议、矛盾的部门，但它们合作得非常好。所以，你在构建非常漂亮的新 UI，但你也使用新 UI 来基本上生成 AI 基础设施和 AI 工作流程，这看起来令人难以置信。其中很多实际上很好地转化回移动应用，并提升了移动体验。它更加对话化，更多是与 Sidekick 谈论你的业务，而不是必须通过界面来操作你的业务。

turns.en: Yep. And previously, before joining Shopify, you were building your own product studio with Molly, and you have incredible motion and animations and interactions there that I always found to be really inspiring. And maybe you can show us some of that and talk through where that came from.
turns.zh: 是的。在加入 Shopify 之前，你与 Molly 一起建立自己的产品工作室，那里有令人难以置信的动效、动画和交互，我一直觉得非常鼓舞人心。也许你可以给我们展示一些，并谈谈它的来源。

turns.en: Yeah, Molly was a studio, a design studio in Brooklyn that I was running together with J Tal, my studio partner. We ran the studio for about 2 years before joining Shopify and integrating the studio into Shopify.
turns.zh: 是的，Molly 是一家工作室，一家位于布鲁克林的设计工作室，我和我的工作室合伙人 J Tal 一起经营。我们在加入 Shopify 并将工作室整合到 Shopify 之前经营了大约两年。

turns.en: And you had some huge clients that you worked with during that time.
turns.zh: 在那段时间里，你有一些巨大的客户合作。

turns.en: Yeah, we worked a lot with Collins and Apple and Google. And also a lot of smaller clients, too. It was honestly a broad mix of web design and product design and a lot of content strategy and hierarchy for clients as well when it came to their websites. And because we were a small studio, it also allowed us to have extremely close relationships with our clients. We would meet clients weekly for many weeks and use these projects at Molly as very high-focus stints with these clients. So we never took on more than two or three clients at a time to stay really focused. Here's just a reel of some of the work we were doing while we were running our studio.
turns.zh: 是的，我们和 Collins、Apple、Google 都有大量合作，也有很多小客户。说实话，业务范围很广，包括网页设计、产品设计，以及为客户网站做内容策略和层级结构。因为我们是小工作室，所以能和客户保持极其紧密的关系。我们会连续多周每周和客户见面，把在 Molly 的这些项目当作与客户高度专注的合作阶段。所以我们一次最多只接两三个客户，以保持专注。这里是一段我们运营工作室期间所做作品的集锦。

turns.en: Cool. There's little details here. The animations are very organic. And even as each screen changes, the gradient and the shadow behind it changes to match the color of the background. I think a lot of people maybe wouldn't pick up on that, but it's something that you sort of intuitively feel something is happening here, right?
turns.zh: 很酷。这里有些小细节。动画非常自然。甚至每个屏幕切换时，渐变和背后的阴影都会变化，以匹配背景颜色。我觉得很多人可能不会注意到，但你会直觉地感觉到这里有些东西在发生，对吧？

turns.en: We got this idea basically just from the ambient lighting behind TVs that are mounted on walls. And I think J Tal, and this was pre-AI, basically duplicated the video and had it blur it out in the background so that it would match the rhythm of what's going on on the screen. And it works really nice. And before this sentence it used to just say Molly is a design studio in Brooklyn, and there was just the gradient at the bottom that was kind of vibrating. It feels like a thunder or something. And at least for us it always felt like people were inclined to scroll into it. So we didn't even have to show them any of the work, but we kind of hinted at it. And then you scrolled into the real, and yeah, the rest are just very nice and simple carousels, but yeah, you can see here this was some of the work we were doing with our studio. And I think some of the patterns you were referring to, we used to call the system we call the system primal. It's a way to just basically understand content on a website, digest content on a website. And for us it was a very structured way of digesting when clients came to us with a lot of information for their websites. We helped them build that into a system on the website that allowed users to explore. To us it always felt like the way we would build websites, and you would flow through the website, felt more like you were exploring the website than the website was demanding your attention. Everything is just one layer away, and everything is progressively disclosed. So you never overwhelm the user with too much content in general.
turns.zh: 这个想法基本上来自挂在墙上的电视背后的环境光。J Tal 在 AI 之前就基本复制了视频，并在背景中模糊处理，使其与屏幕上的节奏相匹配。效果非常好。在这句话之前，它只是说 Molly 是布鲁克林的一家设计工作室，底部只有一种振动的渐变。感觉像雷声什么的。至少对我们来说，它总是让人觉得人们倾向于滚动进去。所以我们甚至不需要向他们展示任何作品，但我们暗示了它。然后你滚动进入真实内容，是的，其余只是非常漂亮简单的轮播，但你可以看到这里是我们工作室的一些作品。我想你提到的一些模式，我们过去称之为系统，我们称之为原始系统。这是一种基本上理解网站内容、消化网站内容的方式。对我们来说，当客户带着大量网站信息来找我们时，这是一种非常有结构的消化方式。我们帮助他们将其构建到网站上的系统中，让用户探索。对我们来说，我们构建网站的方式，你在网站上流动的方式，感觉更像是你在探索网站，而不是网站在要求你的注意力。一切都在一层之外，一切都在逐步披露。所以你永远不会让用户被太多内容淹没。

turns.en: What are some of the ways that you accomplish that?
turns.zh: 你们通过哪些方式实现这一点？

turns.en: I mean, I can just go through some of the work. This was a project we did with the agency Collins. We worked with them for I think over a year on this website. And as you can see, even as you're scrolling through the home page here, each section of the home page is a chapter that as you interact with the website can lead you into further exploration. So this is one of my favorite sections here. This is the bookshelf. These are basically all of the case studies from Collins.
turns.zh: 我的意思是，我可以直接过一遍一些作品。这是我们与 Collins 机构合作的一个项目。我们和他们在这个网站上合作了我想超过一年。如你所见，即使你在这里滚动首页，首页的每个部分都是一个章节，当你与网站互动时，可以引导你进一步探索。所以这是我最喜欢的部分之一。这是书架。这些基本上都是 Collins 的所有案例研究。

turns.en: Even go back and hover over those elements again. The way they bounce feels different than what you typically see.
turns.zh: 甚至回去再悬停那些元素。它们弹跳的方式感觉和通常看到的不同。

turns.en: Yeah. Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。是的。

turns.en: Talk about how you made that. This was you didn't use AI tooling to do this. You hand crafted these, right?
turns.zh: 谈谈你是怎么做的。这不是用 AI 工具做的。这些是你手工制作的，对吧？

turns.en: Yes. Well, in this case I will say this was very much design and engineering partner together. I would lay something like this out in Figma and try to understand the spacing and the size and the colors and the rows and all of that. And then I would hand it off to someone like Jesper who would then work on like the bounce animation for instance. Like all these books have to level up on top of each other and then basically land one more time as the last book kind of lands on top of it and that has to feel very organic because if that feels bouncy and organic then it dilutes at the idea of oh, it's a book. It's a bookshelf that's alive. And those things I think while they are seemingly unimportant are exactly the kind of little moments people pick up when they scroll through these kind of websites.
turns.zh: 是的。嗯，在这种情况下，我会说这非常需要设计和工程合作。我会在 Figma 中布置这样的东西，尝试理解间距、大小、颜色、行等所有内容。然后我会把它交给像 Jesper 这样的人，然后他会处理比如弹跳动画。就像所有这些书必须相互堆叠，然后基本上再落一次，当最后一本书落在上面时，那必须感觉非常自然，因为如果感觉有弹性和自然，那么它会稀释哦，这是一本书的想法。这是一个活的书架。我认为这些事情虽然看似不重要，但正是人们在滚动这些网站时捕捉到的那种小瞬间。

turns.en: That matter? Like you have a person who is supremely talented, whose entire job on this project was to make the tab interaction. And it's very easy for anybody to go, well, just throw a tab. Tabs exist. You can get that for free in 5 seconds and then move on to the next thing. Why did you feel like it was important enough to spend somebody's dedicated time before AI could do this certainly and have them focus just on that one interaction?
turns.zh: 那很重要吗？比如你有一个非常有才华的人，他在这个项目中的全部工作就是制作标签交互。任何人很容易说，好吧，就扔一个标签。标签是存在的。你可以在 5 秒内免费获得，然后继续下一个事情。为什么你觉得在 AI 肯定能做到之前，值得花某个人的专门时间，让他们只专注于那一个交互？

turns.en: There's multiple different ways to answer that, but I think especially for this studio because they work on design themselves. Like this is a branding studio. I think the clients coming to the website are looking for those kind of Easter eggs. They want to know that if I hire this agency or if this agency takes this much detail to produce a website of that quality, what kind of Easter eggs are they going to put into our projects when we work with them? And when they pick our color palette, maybe they're going to come up with a system behind it rather than just picking five colors that they like because that's the level of dedication it takes to go really deep. It's a way to in a way almost also to show off and show the level of craft and detail that you can bring to any piece of or any part of the interface. We try to do the same level of care and craft at Shopify.
turns.zh: 有多种不同的方式回答，但我认为特别是对于这个工作室，因为他们自己从事设计。就像这是一个品牌工作室。我认为来到网站的客户正在寻找那种彩蛋。他们想知道，如果我雇佣这个机构，或者如果这个机构花这么多细节来制作那种质量的网站，那么当我们与他们合作时，他们会在我们的项目中放入什么样的彩蛋？当他们选择我们的调色板时，也许他们会想出背后的系统，而不是仅仅挑选他们喜欢的五种颜色，因为那是真正深入所需的奉献程度。在某种程度上，这也几乎是一种炫耀和展示你可以为界面的任何部分带来的工艺和细节水平的方式。我们在 Shopify 也尝试做同样水平的关怀和工艺。

turns.en: Talk about the decision then to sell your design studio to Shopify and to come join them and how that process has been different for you being at a large public company and you know, leading a product studio internal there versus the work that you were doing here when you were independent.
turns.zh: 那么谈谈将你的设计工作室卖给 Shopify 并加入他们的决定，以及这个过程对你来说有什么不同，在一家大型上市公司，领导内部产品工作室，与你在独立时在这里所做的工作相比。

turns.en: Tobi at the beginning at some point last year basically said, "We're entering a new era and that future needs to be designed." And that was basically it. He's like, "I want to design I want to design for the future and I need to hire good designers who can help me paint a picture and when we see that picture we'll know what it is and we can go down that road." And I think that was the mandate at Shopify like design is very much more in the foreground. It's a very honest organization that's very self-aware. It's a founder-led, engineering-led organization and design hasn't always played the role that it's playing now.
turns.zh: Tobi 在去年某个时候开始基本上说：“我们正在进入一个新时代，那个未来需要被设计。”基本上就是这样。他说：“我想设计，我想为未来设计，我需要雇佣优秀的设计师来帮助我描绘一幅图景，当我们看到那幅图景时，我们会知道它是什么，然后我们可以走上那条路。”我认为这就是 Shopify 的使命，设计更加处于 foreground。这是一个非常诚实的组织，非常自我意识。这是一个创始人领导、工程领导的组织，设计并不总是扮演现在这样的角色。

turns.en: Design is very much helping shape the narrative of where the company is going and the level of craft and pride we're taking towards the tooling and the software that we're building for our merchants. That's beautiful to see, and that was one of the reasons we wanted to join, because we felt that while we were having fun designing websites for other studios like Collins or Spencer the illustrator, we also wanted to have a larger impact and see if our strategy would hold up on interface paradigms with millions of users versus the few users that would scroll around the Spencer website.
turns.zh: 设计在很大程度上帮助塑造了公司发展方向的叙事，以及我们对为商家构建的工具和软件所投入的工艺水平和自豪感。这很美好，这也是我们想加入的原因之一，因为我们觉得，虽然我们为其他工作室如 Collins 或插画家 Spencer 设计网站很有趣，但我们也想产生更大的影响，看看我们的策略在面向数百万用户的界面范式上是否成立，而不是像 Spencer 网站那样只有少数用户浏览。

turns.en: Right. And so it's a different set of challenges. The design studio work that you did was create a new site or something to display work or work on a product or something like that. Talk about how it's different now. Shopify has millions of users and there's a lot of money at stake with every design decision and interaction that you work on. What is your process like now being this internal design studio, and how do you interface with the rest of the organization, and how do you interface with users especially too?
turns.zh: 对。所以这是一组不同的挑战。你之前的设计工作室工作是创建一个新网站或展示作品的东西，或者开发一个产品之类的。谈谈现在有什么不同。Shopify 有数百万用户，你所做的每一个设计决策和交互都涉及大量资金。作为这个内部设计工作室，你现在的流程是怎样的？你如何与组织其他部分对接？尤其是你如何与用户对接？

turns.en: So I will say basically for now our studio exclusively operates within Sidekick, which is the AI infrastructure layer of Shopify. The whole team works extremely close with the rest of the design organization, and it's a very beautiful interplay, which is I think in general how these studios work or how this works more successfully. I've been in positions in previous careers where if you're more isolated, it's always more difficult to ingest into the company and have a large impact in the company. I think at the moment we're very ingrained in the current workflows and ingrained in the timelines and in our road map. And it just requires a lot of experimentation. Honestly, like up-leveling the interface was easy for us because we have really talented designers who rebuild parts of the interface in Figma and then using AI, we're able to port that over into very tangible prototypes extremely quickly. And as we all know, prototypes are a million times more useful than any PRD document you can write. Those spread around the company like wildfire. And if Toby sees a prototype that he likes, then we can go off and build that. And I feel with some of the AI mutations work we've been looking at at Shopify, we can show some of that later. It feels the same. We have ideas in our head, and it's extremely easy for us right now using the current technology to just simulate it all and generate prototypes. Where in the past at Molly, a lot of the work we were doing was by hand. Our sheets were designed by hand. All the animations were done by our developers. Our direction might have been my idea, but other than that, there's like a thousand counterparts that you have to interact with. Right now, I'm seeing one-off armies or teams of two going off and doing the work of many because the tooling is just allowing us to do that. And that's making it a lot easier to get buy-in because I can show up with a prototype and get people's attention faster than I can if I have an idea and I have to get a whole team rallied around an idea.
turns.zh: 所以基本上目前我们的工作室只在 Sidekick 内运作，Sidekick 是 Shopify 的 AI 基础设施层。整个团队与设计组织的其他部分合作非常紧密，这是一种非常美妙的互动，我认为这通常是这些工作室的运作方式，或者更成功的运作方式。在我之前的职业生涯中，我处于更孤立的位置，那样总是更难融入公司并在公司中产生大的影响。我认为目前我们非常深入地融入当前的工作流程、时间线和路线图中。这需要大量的实验。老实说，提升界面对我们来说很容易，因为我们有非常有才华的设计师，他们在 Figma 中重建部分界面，然后使用 AI，我们能够非常快速地将之转化为非常具体的原型。众所周知，原型比你能写的任何 PRD 文档有用一百万倍。这些原型在公司内像野火一样传播。如果 Toby 看到一个他喜欢的原型，我们就可以去构建它。我觉得我们在 Shopify 关注的一些 AI 突变工作，我们稍后可以展示一些。感觉是一样的。我们头脑中有想法，现在使用当前技术非常容易模拟一切并生成原型。而在过去，在 Molly 时，我们做的很多工作都是手工的。我们的图纸是手工设计的。所有动画都是由我们的开发人员完成的。我们的方向可能是我的想法，但除此之外，还有成千上万的对应物需要交互。现在，我看到单兵作战或两人团队在做许多人的工作，因为工具允许我们这样做。这使得获得支持变得容易得多，因为我可以带着原型出现并更快地引起人们的注意，而不是我有一个想法并必须让整个团队围绕一个想法团结起来。

turns.en: Could you show us some of the work that you guys have been building at Shopify?
turns.zh: 你能给我们展示一些你们在 Shopify 一直在构建的工作吗？

turns.en: This is basically a redesign and facelift of our current admin experience with a new home design and an overall facelift of basically the entire product which we've been working on at the moment. I think one of the more interesting things that we've been exploring right now is just how Sidekick and the merchant interact with each other. We have this concept of Sidekick suggestions on the home feed. These suggestions are brought to the merchant by us. We've identified opportunities and benefits that the merchant could do inside of their ecosystem, inside of their universe, and we can show those to the user and then as the user interacts with these suggestions, we basically kick off a conversation with Sidekick. We can directly manipulate the admin dashboard for the user and we can show those changes to a user. So, we're showing a user right here. We think you should rewrite or re-rewrite the description of your product. Here's the suggestion that we think you should do. You can publish these changes and basically through a conversation with Sidekick, you've directly manipulated your store and the concept is more can we bring UI to the user and into context versus having the user click through the interface. At the end of the day, there's a world where a merchant can spend a lot more time on the home surface and use Shopify as a dashboard to delegate and interact with Sidekick and have Sidekick directly manipulate the store. Right now, what you're looking at is still a prototype environment. This is there's a dev UI panel inside here and basically we are building all of these the design team is building all of these changes and demos and ideas right into the interface here so we can just test and build on top of it and it's become this beautiful process where once a demo is at a point where we kind of all align everybody branches off and builds a version of something that they think that brings value and then we all come back together and it actually lives all inside the same demo and the same language.
turns.zh: 这基本上是对我们当前管理体验的重新设计和改版，有一个新的主页设计，以及基本上整个产品的全面改版，我们目前正在做这个。我认为我们现在探索的更有趣的事情之一是 Sidekick 和商家如何互动。我们在主页 feed 上有 Sidekick 建议的概念。这些建议由我们带给商家。我们已经确定了商家可以在他们的生态系统内、他们的宇宙内做的机会和好处，我们可以向用户展示这些，然后当用户与这些建议互动时，我们基本上启动与 Sidekick 的对话。我们可以直接为用户操作管理仪表板，并向用户展示这些更改。所以，我们在这里向用户展示。我们认为你应该重写或重新重写你的产品描述。这是我们认为你应该做的建议。你可以发布这些更改，基本上通过与 Sidekick 的对话，你直接操作了你的商店，概念更多的是我们能否将 UI 带给用户并融入上下文，而不是让用户点击界面。归根结底，有一种世界是商家可以在主页面上花费更多时间，并使用 Shopify 作为仪表板来委托并与 Sidekick 互动，让 Sidekick 直接操作商店。现在，你看到的是一个原型环境。这里有一个开发 UI 面板，基本上我们正在构建设计团队正在构建所有这些更改、演示和想法直接进入这里的界面，所以我们可以直接测试并在其上构建，它已经成为这个美丽的过程，一旦演示达到我们都一致的程度，每个人就分头构建他们认为带来价值的某个版本，然后我们都回来，它实际上都生活在同一个演示和同一种语言中。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: And it's just a beautiful way to share ideas and context.
turns.zh: 这是一种分享想法和上下文的美丽方式。

turns.en: You said designers are building this in here. A lot of times designers are designing and they're not building but it's in Shopify and your team and you are building a lot of the stuff that you are designing so that you can test it so you can prototype it so you can see it on live data live experiences and that's a huge part of nailing it and building something useful and making sure that it's great. What was your evolution from you know designing in Figma to now you are not just designing but you're actually creating it out into the world to be able to test it and doing that full loop yourself.
turns.zh: 你说设计师在这里构建这个。很多时候设计师在设计，但他们不构建，但在 Shopify，你的团队和你正在构建很多你设计的东西，这样你可以测试它，可以原型化它，可以看到它在实时数据、实时体验上的表现，这是做好它、构建有用东西并确保它很棒的重要部分。从你在 Figma 中设计到现在你不仅仅是设计，而是实际上将其创造到世界上以能够测试它并自己完成整个循环，你的演变是怎样的？

turns.en: In this specific case admin has a playground that we build inside of that playground we test that's not production code and that wouldn't be allowed back into the main GitHub repo of Shopify into like our main repository. Having said that though AI has definitely gotten to the point now where as designers we are highly empowered and capable to visualize any idea that we want to get our idea across in a previous world that just wasn't possible.
turns.zh: 在这个具体案例中，admin 有一个游乐场，我们在那个游乐场内构建和测试，那不是生产代码，不会被允许回到 Shopify 的主要 GitHub 仓库，比如我们的主仓库。尽管如此，AI 现在肯定已经达到了这样的程度：作为设计师，我们被高度赋能，能够可视化任何我们想要传达想法的想法，而在过去的世界中这是不可能的。

turns.en: We looked at the Collins website earlier. A lot of that work in Figma, when we worked on it, still looks like this. You can zoom into any part here and they're highly detailed Figma screens that we were designing through. This is an ideation process. I think this is a mixture of me, Michael Spicer, and J Tall working on this project together. You can just see the evolution as we're going through ideas and trying out new things. These are too heavy and too expensive to test in code. We don't want to test this in code right now because it would require an engineer to take a look at it and build it for us. So we test it all in Figma. Figma is the playground in the world we were building everything in. We were building it on desktop and then translating it to mobile, and all of this had to be stress tested out in Figma first for a very long time before we would go and bug the engineering team.
turns.zh: 我们之前看了 Collins 网站。很多在 Figma 里的工作，我们做的时候，现在看起来还是这样。你可以放大这里的任何部分，都是非常详细的 Figma 屏幕，我们通过它来设计。这是一个构思过程。我觉得这是我、Michael Spicer 和 J Tall 一起做这个项目的混合成果。你可以看到我们推进想法、尝试新事物时的演变。这些在代码里测试太重、太贵。我们现在不想在代码里测试，因为那需要工程师来看并为我们构建。所以我们在 Figma 里全部测试。Figma 是我们构建一切的世界里的游乐场。我们在桌面端构建，然后移植到移动端，所有这些都必须先在 Figma 里压力测试很长时间，然后我们才会去打扰工程团队。

ts.sec: Using AI as a design tool

turns.en: A lot of the way I'm talking to AI or I'm still using Figma at the moment is I can get really far with a very broad sketch. Here's an example of a side project I've been working on over the weekend, which I can go into detail a bit. One of the things I wanted to build out for this project was a 2x3 overview of these grass studies and these videos I took. The interaction here is you can open up any one of these videos and you can drag down to close them. It works the same in the simulator. I explained this, I described this to AI, and I was working in Codex, and Codex built this out for me. But the interaction wasn't interruptible. So every time I clicked on an asset and pulled it down, I had to wait until the asset was all the way back in its position and set down before I was able to tap on another image, and that's just not how you want to use this pattern. This has to be very responsive, very quickly, otherwise you'll get very annoyed with the interface very fast. So I just went into Figma and drew out very rudimentary simple boxes: when you click on the box, red comes up. You can swipe it away. If as you're swiping it away, you click on blue, blue now comes up. And you can click that away and you do it with green. And I think that's just a good example of how at least myself personally I'm using Figma more. It's more of a scratch pad to map out ideas and I give those ideas to Codex. I use the scratchpad because it's easier for me to decompile something, but also it's actually easy for Codex to decompile it if it sees it visually. It interprets that image, I think similar to how I interpreted it. At least it understood what I was doing and how I was thinking about the motion. I couldn't articulate it via text or voice, but I could draw it out.
turns.zh: 目前我与 AI 交流或仍在使用 Figma 的很多方式是，我可以通过非常粗略的草图走得很远。这里有一个我周末一直在做的副项目示例，我可以稍微详细讲讲。我想为这个项目构建的一个东西是这些草地研究和视频的 2x3 概览。这里的交互是，你可以打开这些视频中的任何一个，然后向下拖动来关闭它们。在模拟器里也是一样的。我向 AI 解释、描述了这个，当时我在用 Codex，Codex 为我构建了这个。但交互不可中断。所以每次我点击一个资产并向下拉，我都必须等到资产完全回到原位并落定，才能点击另一张图片，而这根本不是你想使用这种模式的方式。这必须非常快速响应，否则你很快就会对界面感到非常恼火。所以我只是进入 Figma，画出了非常基础的简单方框：当你点击方框时，红色出现。你可以把它滑走。如果你在滑走时点击蓝色，蓝色就会出现。你可以把它点走，然后用绿色做同样的事。我认为这只是一个很好的例子，说明至少我个人是如何更多地使用 Figma 的。它更像是一个草稿本，用来规划想法，然后我把这些想法交给 Codex。我使用草稿本是因为对我来说更容易分解某件事，而且如果 Codex 视觉上看到它，它实际上也很容易分解。它解读那张图像，我认为类似于我解读它的方式。至少它理解我在做什么以及我如何思考运动。我无法通过文字或语音表达出来，但我可以画出来。

turns.en: There's two parts of this that I think are important to call out. I think number one, Codex and all the current AI software and the models are extremely capable at creating anything. You can use these tools to make anything that you want, but you have to know what you're doing and you have to be able to take a concept or something more complicated like the shader and break it down into all its little components. You have to be able to understand those commands and then you can put those components back together.
turns.zh: 我认为这里面有两点很重要，需要指出。第一，Codex 和所有当前的 AI 软件以及模型在创造任何东西方面都极其强大。你可以用这些工具做出任何你想要的东西，但你必须知道你在做什么，你必须能够把一个概念或更复杂的东西（比如着色器）分解成所有的小组件。你必须能够理解那些命令，然后你才能把这些组件重新组合起来。

turns.en: Yeah, just show us how you did that here. So to be clear, you had a bunch of images and videos of actual grass. And then you wanted to create a shader that looked identical to that, but you could control and function like a shader. And so talk about how the different elements and what you had to go through to actually get that to look lifelike.
turns.zh: 是的，就给我们展示一下你在这里是怎么做的。所以明确一下，你有一堆真实草地的图片和视频。然后你想创建一个看起来和它一模一样，但你可以控制并且像着色器一样运作的着色器。所以谈谈不同的元素，以及你经历了什么才真正让它看起来逼真。

turns.en: I have a few screenshots here. Again, this is a good example of how I use Figma. So I fed the video into Codex for the first time and just explained the project and the process that I wanted to go through. Take the video, turn this into a shader. I want the shader running in the web, and I want you to be as meticulous as you can. Be very pixel perfect. Grab all the colors. Make sure that you're using the same hex codes. Understand each part of the image and then try to recreate that. And it went off and said, "No problem. I got you." and it came up with this, which obviously doesn't look at all where we landed, where we ended up now. But then the process from here was I would screenshot this and my original video. I would open up ChatGPT and I gave it to another agent there. I explained that agent exactly what I was doing as well as why is the other agent not understanding what I'm trying to get to. And that ChatGPT then helped me understand my own process like, well, you have to explain to it where the light is coming from and what shadows you're using and maybe break the image actually down into like six parts and have it do each one of those individually and put that back together. And as I was thinking about all of these different things, I was trying to come up with how could I become very clear with AI and explain to it exactly what it was actually looking at. So one of the tricks I used was I went into ChatGPT and I had it render basically a topographical map of the underlying structure. As I was going through this, it was getting closer and you could see that it was painting more pixels into the grass blades. Yeah, these started to look like bushels a little bit, which felt more realistic and then over here I was like, okay, we're getting somewhere here now. This doesn't look terrible anymore. But I kind of figured out it doesn't understand that there's not a flat layer underneath. These are little hills.
turns.zh: 我这里有几张截图。再次，这是我如何使用 Figma 的一个好例子。所以我第一次把视频输入 Codex，并解释了项目和我想要经历的过程。拿这个视频，把它变成着色器。我想要着色器在网页上运行，我希望你尽可能细致。非常像素级完美。抓取所有颜色。确保你使用相同的十六进制代码。理解图像的每个部分，然后尝试重现它。它跑开并说：“没问题。交给我。”然后它做出了这个，显然看起来完全不像我们现在达到的结果。但接下来的过程是，我会截图这个和我原始的视频。我会打开 ChatGPT，把它交给那里的另一个智能体。我向那个智能体解释我在做什么，以及为什么另一个智能体不理解我想要达到的目标。然后那个 ChatGPT 帮助我理解我自己的过程，比如，你必须向它解释光来自哪里，你使用什么阴影，也许把图像实际分解成六个部分，让它分别处理每个部分，然后再组合起来。当我在思考所有这些不同的事情时，我试图想出如何与 AI 变得非常清晰，并向它解释它实际看到的是什么。所以我使用的一个技巧是，我进入 ChatGPT，让它渲染出底层结构的地形图。当我经历这个过程时，它越来越接近，你可以看到它在草叶中绘制了更多像素。是的，这些开始看起来有点像草丛，感觉更真实了，然后到这里我想，好的，我们有点进展了。这看起来不再那么糟糕了。但我有点发现它不理解下面不是平坦的一层。这些是小山丘。

turns.en: Right.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: Basically, I fed this back into AI and it understood, oh, okay. So there's an underlying structure and a map that has different depths and heights and if I can render the grass on top of that infrastructure or of that structure in general, it'll be much easier for me to create the scene and that kind of worked really well and you know, in this prototype reference you can actually buy there's a binary toggle to turn the grass on or off and you can actually play with the terrain quite a bit here as well.
turns.zh: 基本上，我把这个反馈给 AI，它理解了，哦，好的。所以有一个底层结构和一张有不同深度和高度地图，如果我能把草渲染在那个基础设施或那个结构之上，对我来说创建场景就会容易得多，这确实效果很好，你知道，在这个原型参考中你实际上可以买——有一个二元切换开关来打开或关闭草，你实际上也可以在这里玩很多地形。

turns.en: Right.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: This was all unlocked via Josh to me at a lunch the other day where he kind of like we installed DialKit into this demo because he looked at this and like this looks pretty good, but you should look at the length of the grass blades. I was like, whoa, okay, that's true.
turns.zh: 这一切都是前几天午餐时 Josh 对我解锁的，他把 DialKit 安装到这个演示中，因为他看着这个说，这看起来不错，但你应该看看草叶的长度。我当时想，哇，好的，确实如此。

turns.en: So, I asked Codex like, hey, how many grass blade variations do we have? And it said we have about 217,000 different grass blades, but they only differ by like 0.7, 0.8. So, we were like, okay, let's just build a toggle for it so that we can see it ourselves. I don't want to have to go back and forth with the interface and chat about this. Expose the underlying structure. Exposing the underlying structure would also show me where I had made mistakes. The original version of the terrain map that I had implemented was completely wrong and skewed. So, I couldn't get to my outcome anyway because I had misinterpreted something five prompts ago that I didn't know about anyway. DialKit kind of unpack that for me. But then in general you can just mess with a few of these values and they kind of help bring some of this, they help visualize what I really wanted to see. And if the length here is longer, you can introduce more wind. This was something I wanted to test and see how crazy I could get with the wind movement. You can see it gets a little wild. But yeah, I think this is just a small example of a little bit of a fun project just to try and see how far can you get with the tools. And these are things that I think before AI I couldn't do. I just might have had these ideas but I wasn't allowed or able to execute on them. And I think that's just in general what's changing with a lot of the design role right now. And anyway, designers are becoming more full stack. As are engineers and PMs. It goes in every which way.

ts.sec: Critique of Tabs and Feature Overload

turns.en: And you, I feel like have an interesting approach on tabs because all those sliders that you make, they're effectively like tabs, right? It's just you have the affordance of knowing that there are multiple of them and you can see multiple at a time.
turns.zh: 而你，我觉得你对标签页有一种有趣的思路，因为你做的那些滑块，它们实际上就像标签页，对吧？只是你有一种可供性，知道有多个滑块，并且可以同时看到多个。

turns.en: Yeah.

turns.en: And I feel like the trap that a lot of people fall into a lot of times with tabs like these is people users usually will not click on all of the tabs and explore them all. And so, you have to assume that whatever is hidden behind all of them, nobody will ever see. How do you think about that? And how can they encourage people to explore this more and get more information rather than burying everything behind tabs?
turns.zh: 我觉得很多人在使用这样的标签页时经常陷入的陷阱是，用户通常不会点击所有标签页并探索它们全部。所以，你必须假设隐藏在所有标签页后面的内容，没有人会看到。你如何看待这一点？他们如何鼓励人们更多地探索并获取更多信息，而不是把所有东西都埋在标签页后面？

turns.en: There's this rule I always have like you can't put more than seven lines of text on a slide if you're presenting work. Like you have to come up with almost rules and constraints of how many features you want to show off. Like a good example I think I would use a three up component here. I would take all of these features. I would compress this information down and try to understand what are the top three things that Skill Synch can do for you. You can do X, Y, and Z. Those are the three things you show off. All of those are tappable. They lead you into potentially sheets or a view transition into more information. And then you have more context behind. Since it's very flat and broad, you're kind of like a mile wide but only an inch deep. You don't really know what you're really looking at. That's what that requires like a deeper understanding of your feature set and then more condensing those down into principles and rules and main kind of like points. And then you can rally or bring more information under each of those kind of pillars. And that'll help the users understand the flow of the website better and how to navigate it. consensus.en: Designers are now editors: AI handles execution, humans curate and set the bar.
consensus.zh: 设计师如今是编辑：AI 负责执行，人类负责筛选和设定标准。

consensus.en: AI raises the ceiling but doesn't know what looks good; human judgment remains essential.
consensus.zh: AI 提高了上限，但不知道什么好看；人类判断仍不可或缺。

consensus.en: Prototypes built with AI spread faster and are more persuasive than PRD documents.
consensus.zh: 用 AI 构建的原型传播更快，比 PRD 文档更有说服力。

consensus.en: Break complex tasks into subtasks and feed them to AI agents iteratively.
consensus.zh: 将复杂任务分解为子任务，迭代地喂给 AI 智能体。

consensus.en: Expose underlying parameters with tools like DialKit to fine-tune AI-generated designs.
consensus.zh: 用 DialKit 等工具暴露底层参数，微调 AI 生成的设计。

consensus.en: Progressive disclosure and clear hierarchy are key to good design, especially with AI.
consensus.zh: 渐进披露和清晰层级是优秀设计的关键，在 AI 时代尤其如此。

contrarian.en: AI is an infinitely patient collaborator; iterate 91 times without bothering engineers.
contrarian.zh: AI 是无限耐心的协作者；迭代 91 次也不用麻烦工程师。

contrarian.en: Smooth scrolling and scroll-jacking are disasters; use native scroll for interruptible interfaces.
contrarian.zh: 平滑滚动和滚动劫持是灾难；使用原生滚动实现可中断界面。

contrarian.en: Don't hide content behind tabs; users won't click them—make pages longer instead.
contrarian.zh: 不要把内容藏在标签页后面；用户不会点击——不如让页面更长。

contrarian.en: AI-generated animations often add no value; curation and human craft matter more.
contrarian.zh: AI 生成的动画往往没有价值；筛选和人类技艺更重要。

contrarian.en: Designers should learn to build and test in code, not just design in Figma.
contrarian.zh: 设计师应学会用代码构建和测试，而不仅仅在 Figma 中设计。

contrarian.en: Less is more: reduce features to top three and show them clearly.
contrarian.zh: 少即是多：将功能精简到前三项并清晰展示。
